We’re at the forefront of a once in a generational change in the broadband industry. Join us as we innovate, help our customers reach their potential, and connect underserved communities with unrivaled digital experiences.

The Global Repair Operations & Reverse Logistics Program Manager serves as the global process owner for all Return Material Authorization (RMA), repair, refurbishment, and product recovery activities. This role is responsible for defining, governing, and continuously improving the end-to-end return and repair ecosystem across customers, contract manufacturers, third-party repair providers, logistics partners, suppliers, quality teams, and engineering organizations.


As a senior subject matter expert, this position provides strategic leadership through influence rather than direct personnel management. The role owns process performance, operational governance, partner management, inventory recovery strategies, and service execution to ensure efficient product support throughout the product lifecycle.


The successful candidate will drive operational excellence across warranty returns, depot repair operations, failure analysis workflows, product recovery programs, and supplier corrective action processes while ensuring compliance, traceability, cost optimization, and customer satisfaction.


Key Responsibilities

Global Process Ownership

  • Own and govern the end-to-end RMA process, including customer returns, replacement fulfillment, repair, refurbishment, disposition, supplier returns, and inventory recovery.
  • Define process standards, policies, controls, KPIs, and operating procedures for all return and repair activities.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce cycle times, improve recovery rates, increase repair yields, and lower operational costs.
  • Establish operational governance and performance management frameworks for global return and repair operations.

Repair Operations & Service Partner Management

  • Manage global relationships with third-party repair depots, contract manufacturers, logistics providers, and specialized rework partners.
  • Own repair partner performance, including service levels, turnaround times, quality metrics, cost management, capacity planning, and contractual obligations.
  • Lead quarterly business reviews and operational performance reviews with repair and refurbishment providers.
  • Coordinate deployment of new repair capabilities, test infrastructure, certifications, and repair process improvements.
  • Drive corrective actions and performance improvement plans when supplier or repair partner performance falls below expectations.

RMA Operations & Product Recovery

  • Lead execution of warranty returns, advanced replacements, refurbishment programs, recertification activities, and product recovery initiatives.
  • Own customer-facing RMA operations, including request intake and qualification, return authorization, status communications, escalation support, proactive follow-up on pending and aged returns, recovery of outstanding customer assets, return compliance, and continuous improvement of the customer return experience.
  • Ensure timely disposition of returned product through repair, return to stock, supplier recovery, scrap, engineering analysis, or field replacement.
  • Partner with logistics providers to optimize reverse logistics networks and return material flows.
  • Develop scalable processes to support product launches, lifecycle transitions, recalls, product withdrawals, and end-of-life activities.

Failure Analysis & Quality Management

  • Coordinate cross-functional failure analysis activities involving Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Customer Support, and external service partners.
  • Drive root-cause investigations and corrective action execution for field returns and warranty failures.
  • Support supplier quality initiatives, corrective action programs, and containment activities.
  • Ensure compliance with Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, traceability standards, and regulatory obligations.
  • Monitor product reliability trends and provide recommendations to improve field quality performance.

Inventory Planning & Asset Recovery

  • Develop forecasts for RMA volumes, repair demand, replacement inventory requirements, and recovery yields.
  • Manage repair pipeline inventory, replacement stock, service inventory, and excess recovery opportunities.
  • Partner with Supply Chain and Planning teams to ensure material availability supporting repair and replacement requirements.
  • Establish strategies to maximize asset recovery while minimizing write-offs and inventory obsolescence.

Supplier & Financial Management

  • Manage purchase orders, repair quotations, invoices, component procurement, service contracts, and repair-related budgets.
  • Evaluate supplier performance using operational, quality, financial, and service metrics.
  • Support sourcing and qualification of new repair, rework, and refurbishment partners.

The Role:

The Senior Biomechanist works with engineering staff in human-injury impact analysis in vehicular accidents, reconstructing vehicular accidents, consulting and analysis of injuries related to premises liability and slip-and-fall incidents, and requires extensive experience in forensic biomechanical analyses. This role performs investigations focusing on musculoskeletal biomechanics to determine the relationship between accident modes and injuries and requires evaluation and analysis of biomechanical systems, including voluntary and involuntary human motions, assessment of situations leading to the accident, and reconstructing the accidents. The role requires familiarity with legal depositions, working with attorneys and claims adjusters. Additionally, the ideal candidate has experience working with network of external clientele (e.g. lawyers, insurance carriers and adjusters, etc.) and is experienced with building, establishing, and maintaining rapport with this network. This is a fully remote role open to candidates located anywhere in the United States. Candidates located in the listed states are encouraged to apply.

In This Role, You Will:

Inspect and measures vehicles. Provide expert testimony at trials, depositions, or other legal proceedings and communicates investigative findings in a manner easily understood by technical or non-technical audiences. Use computer models to reconstruct accidents and to measure load and injury levels. Conduct detailed inspections of vehicles and accident sites and accurately analyzes crash sequences to identify contributing factors and the induced loading on the occupants. Review various documents to identify relevant information for an accident reconstruction or biomechanical engineering analysis (includes police reports, medical records, depositions, expert reports, legal pleadings and discovery documents, videos, photographs, etc.) Perform simulations of vehicular collisions using advanced collision reconstruction software such as PC-Crash. Evaluates the effects of impact forces on occupants as a result of vehicular accidents. Determine human injury mechanisms in vehicular accidents and premises liability cases such as slip-and-fall accidents. Perform accident reconstructions of single-vehicle rollovers, single-vehicle impacts with fixed objects, and multi-vehicle collisions (frontal, side, rear, and sideswipe). Utilize engineering principles to calculate factors such as impact and departure speeds, collision forces, and trajectories of vehicles. Compare calculations with crash test reports of similar collisions to correlate damages based on calculated velocities. Review papers and journals related to vehicular accident reconstruction to understand and advance the scientific techniques used in reconstruction work. Provide written conclusions of findings to assist others in understanding the evidence or in determining the facts at issue. Take an active role in marketing YA Engineering Services to clients and to the forensic engineering community.

What You Bring:

4+ years of experience in biomechanics, accident reconstruction, and premises liability work or similar required Degree in Mechanical or Biomedical Engineering required Prior deposition and courtroom testimony experience a plus Experience with CAD related to accident reconstruction PE license, PhD, SAE certification or ACTAR certification Familiarity with automotive engineering and automotive control systems Understanding of billable hours or project-based work Experience collaborating with forensic animators to develop visual exhibits for deposition and trial support Exposure to performing and evaluating computer simulations Based in (or planning to relocate to) the job location Team‑oriented with a strong passion for learning

Who We Are:

YA is an international professional services organization providing forensic consulting, engineering, risk mitigation, and related services. Founded over 25 years ago as a property damage consulting firm, YA has expanded through organic growth and strategic acquisitions. Today, YA has over 800 professionals dedicated to excellence, partnership, and driving innovation. YA Group’s Accident Reconstruction & Biomechanics team applies scientific investigation, engineering principles, and advanced technology to determine how collisions occur and why. Capable of handling the full spectrum of motor vehicle accidents—from low‑speed impacts to complex rollover events, heavy‑truck collisions, autonomous vehicle incidents, and ADAS evaluations—our multidisciplinary specialists deliver analytically grounded findings that support clients across insurance, legal, corporate, and transportation sectors. About Empower Community Care

Empower Community Care is a family of mission-driven organizations delivering evidence-based behavioral health, child welfare, and community care programs and services. Our portfolio includes BSFT, Carey Group, Evidence-Based Associates (EBA), FFT LLC, MST Services, Orbis, and The Incredible Years — each advancing outcomes for children, families, and the communities we serve.

Position Summary

Empower Community Care is seeking a Recruiter to lead full-cycle recruitment across our family of organizations and the customer agencies we support. This remote, enterprise-wide role covers the behavioral health, child welfare, and community care positions our customers hire for, plus corporate, consulting, technical, and operations roles within Empower and its subsidiaries.
Working closely with the Senior Recruiter, internal hiring managers, and customer agency leaders, the Recruiter will assess hiring needs, build talent pipelines, screen and advance qualified candidates, and deliver a candidate experience that reflects our mission. The ideal candidate is organized, consultative, and comfortable running many varied searches across states while staying compliant with hiring laws. The Senior Recruiter provides day-to-day recruiting direction, workload prioritization, and performance coaching, while the HR Manager supports employment compliance matters.

Key Responsibilities

  • Full-Cycle Recruiting: Manage assigned searches from intake through hand-off to onboarding, including sourcing, screening, interview coordination, and offer and background check support, for customer agency and internal positions.
  • Hiring Needs Assessment: Work with customer agency leaders and Empower hiring managers to clarify requirements, timelines, and sourcing strategy, and advise on market conditions and candidate supply with the HR Manager. Serve as a primary recruiting point of contact for assigned hiring managers and customer agencies, providing regular pipeline updates, identifying hiring challenges, and recommending adjustments to recruitment strategies.
  • Sourcing & Pipeline Development: Build talent pipelines for recurring and hard-to-fill roles (clinical, program, supervisory, consulting, training, corporate, technical, and operations positions) through job boards, professional networks, social media, university and association partners, community organizations, and job fairs and networking events you manage and attend. Proactively identify and engage passive candidates through targeted outreach, referrals, LinkedIn Recruiter or similar tools, and creative sourcing strategies.
  • Screening & Candidate Experience: Conduct structured phone and video screens using consistent, job-related criteria, assess qualifications, credentials, and fit, and present qualified candidates to hiring managers with clear recommendations. Communicate promptly and respectfully at every stage, including timely notice of outcomes, in keeping with our mission-driven culture.
  • Postings & Requisitions: Publish accurate job postings with the Senior Recruiter, including required pay transparency and EEO language, and manage requisitions and candidate records in the applicant tracking system (ATS). Maintain accurate and timely documentation of candidate statuses, interview feedback, hiring decisions, and recruitment activities to support transparent processes and consistent reporting.
  • Hiring Compliance: Apply federal, state, and local hiring laws across a multi-state workforce, including EEO, pay transparency, fair chance, background check (FCRA), and I-9 eligibility rules; escalate questions to the HR Manager.
  • Metrics & Process Improvement: Report metrics such as time-to-fill, time-to-submit, pipeline health, interview activity, source effectiveness, offer acceptance, and hiring manager and customer satisfaction; provide regular updates on assigned searches, identify recruiting barriers, and use data to refine plans and improve processes, tools, templates, and employer brand consistency across Empower and its subsidiaries.

Required Qualifications

  • Experience: Minimum of three (3) years of full-cycle recruiting experience, preferably in a high-volume or multi-role environment with responsibility for multiple concurrent requisitions.
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in human resources, business, psychology, communications, or a related field, or equivalent education and experience.
  • Sourcing, Screening & Technology: Demonstrated ability to source active and passive candidates and evaluate them using structured, job-related criteria, with working proficiency in an ATS, job boards, LinkedIn or similar tools, Microsoft 365, and video-conferencing platforms. Experience with JazzHR or a comparable ATS is a plus.
  • Communication & Relationship Skills: Strong verbal and written communication, cultural competence, and discretion with confidential information, with the ability to work consultatively with hiring managers, customer agency leaders, and candidates from varied backgrounds.
  • Organization & Prioritization: Strong attention to detail; ability to independently manage a dynamic portfolio of searches across roles, locations, and deadlines, adapt to changing priorities, meet agreed-upon recruiting timelines, and maintain consistent communication with candidates and hiring managers across time zones.
  • Employment Law Knowledge: Working knowledge of EEO, pay transparency, background check, and fair hiring requirements, and the ability to apply multi-state rules with HR guidance.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Behavioral Health & Human Services Recruiting: Experience recruiting licensed and master’s-level clinical professionals, including therapists, counselors, social workers, clinical supervisors, and community-based program staff in behavioral health, child welfare, or human services, as well as corporate, technical, and operations roles. Familiarity with clinical licensure requirements and evidence-based programs such as MST, FFT, and BSFT is highly desirable.
  • Client-Facing Recruiting: Experience recruiting for external clients, such as in a staffing, agency, or recruitment process outsourcing environment.
  • Multi-State Hiring: Experience hiring remote employees across multiple states and managing state-specific posting and pay transparency requirements.
  • Data & Certification: Comfort building simple recruiting reports and dashboards in Excel or a similar tool; SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, SPHR, or a recognized talent acquisition certification.

Additional Requirements

  • Background Check: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check, consistent with applicable law and Empower’s standard hiring practices.
  • Confidentiality: This role may involve exposure to confidential organizational, candidate, financial, and/or program information. The employee must maintain strict confidentiality and comply with Empower’s internal data governance and confidentiality policies.
  • Work Environment: This is a remote, computer-based position requiring prolonged periods of sitting and extended use of a computer, keyboard, and video-conferencing tools, along with travel of up to approximately 10% of the time for job fairs, in-person meetings, or customer site visits. Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities in accordance with the ADA.
  • Other Duties: This job description reflects the general nature and level of work performed and is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Benefits

Empower Community Care offers a competitive total-rewards package, which includes medical, dental, and vision coverage; retirement savings; paid time off and holidays; and life insurance.

About Modern Executive Solutions

Modern Executive Solutions is a fully integrated talent management consultancy with a specific focus on developing diverse, modern leadership teams. We provide services that include talent and organization strategy, culture and change management, leadership assessment and development and executive search. Everything we do is forward-looking and focused on creating modern organizations, leadership team and leaders. We are headquartered out of Atlanta, Georgia but work on a remote-first basis with employees across the United States and a team also in the United Kingdom. As a part of our embedded purpose to change lives for the better we donate 10% of our annual profits to charities that support youth and education in order to develop the diverse talent of tomorrow.

About the Role

Modern’s mission is to partner with the world’s leading organizations to reimagine and implement a modern approach to leadership and talent. We connect the development of leaders and leadership teams with the culture and organizational conditions that enable them to succeed.

As a Managing Director in our Consulting Practice, you will lead work spanning leadership assessment, leadership development, team effectiveness, and culture. Leadership development will be your primary focus, with assessment providing insight to inform development priorities, coaching, and broader talent decisions.

Your work will encompass both tailored client consulting engagements and the ongoing development and expansion of Modern’s leadership academies. Across these settings, you will translate business and leadership challenges into practical solutions and development experiences that strengthen capability and support sustained behavior change.

Your primary accountability will be leading high-quality engagements and developing trusted executive relationships through the work. You will shape solutions, lead consulting teams, manage delivery and engagement economics, and ensure our work creates measurable value. Through that impact, you will strengthen client loyalty, support retention, and identify opportunities to deepen and expand our partnerships.

Working alongside our Partners, you will contribute subject matter expertise to business development, including client discussions, solution design, proposals, scoping, and pricing. Partners will lead sales pursuits, with your contribution bringing specialist insight and delivery credibility.

This role suits a hands-on consulting leader who combines thoughtful client counsel with disciplined engagement management, develops colleagues, and takes ownership of the client and participant experience.

What You’ll Do

Engagement Management and Leadership Consulting

  • Lead engagements spanning leadership assessment, development, team effectiveness, and culture, integrating these disciplines where they strengthen client outcomes.
  • Translate client priorities into clear outcomes, solution designs, workplans, and measures of impact.
  • Design and deliver tailored leadership assessment and development programs, executive workshops, and leadership team engagements.
  • Facilitate senior groups confidently, helping participants generate insight, build alignment, and commit to practical action.
  • Help clients connect leadership expectations and behaviors with their desired culture and business strategy.
  • Incorporate assessment, feedback, coaching, and workplace application into coherent development journeys, contributing directly to assessment delivery within your expertise.
  • Coordinate consulting colleagues and specialists into an integrated solution with clear responsibilities and consistent delivery standards.
  • Manage scope, timelines, budgets, resources, and profitability, anticipating risks and resolving issues early.

Leadership Academies

  • Support the ongoing development and expansion of Modern’s leadership academies through program design, content development, facilitation, and continuous improvement.
  • Work with colleagues, faculty, coaches, and executive contributors to create relevant, connected development experiences.
  • Connect assessment insights, individual development priorities, cohort learning, and practical application throughout the participant journey.
  • Contribute learning from client consulting to academy programming and apply relevant academy insights to client work.
  • Evaluate participant feedback and development outcomes to strengthen program quality, relevance, and impact.

Executive Relationships, Retention and Expansion

  • Develop trusted relationships with executive sponsors, senior stakeholders, and participants through the quality of your counsel and delivery.
  • Maintain a clear understanding of stakeholder expectations, business priorities, and how client needs evolve during the work.
  • Lead ongoing client dialogue on progress, insights, outcomes, and emerging needs, addressing concerns directly and constructively.
  • Build continuity beyond individual deliverables through meaningful follow-through, review of results, and discussion of future priorities.
  • Identify opportunities to extend or broaden the work based on demonstrated value and client needs, partnering with the relevant Partner to shape next steps.
  • Strengthen retention and advocacy by ensuring clients experience Modern as an insightful, responsive, and dependable partner.

Business Development Support

  • Participate as a subject matter expert in Partner-led sales discussions, bringing relevant experience, insight, and delivery credibility.
  • Help diagnose prospective client needs and translate them into practical solution designs.
  • Contribute to proposals, presentations, scope development, resource estimates, and pricing.
  • Ensure proposed approaches are deliverable, appropriately resourced, and commercially sound.
  • Support a smooth transition from sales into delivery, maintaining clarity on commitments, expectations, and intended outcomes.

Quality, Team Leadership and Practice Development

  • Take accountability for the rigor, relevance, and quality of work delivered under your leadership.
  • Build solutions around each client’s business context and existing frameworks, drawing on Modern’s intellectual property where it adds value.
  • Lead consulting teams with clear expectations, effective delegation, and timely, developmental feedback.
  • Coach colleagues and strengthen their consulting judgment, facilitation skills, and client management capability.
  • Turn engagement learning into stronger methodologies, tools, offerings, and shared knowledge.
  • Bring fresh thinking on leadership and culture, including thoughtful use of technology and AI to improve insight, delivery, and client value.

Knowledge

  • Leadership Consulting: Applied understanding of advanced leadership science and practices including; measurement, leadership behavior change, executive development, and the design of learning experiences that translate into sustained workplace application.
  • Team effectiveness and culture: Understanding of leadership team dynamics, organizational culture, and how leadership behaviors enable or constrain strategy execution.
  • Talent and organizational context: Understanding of how leadership development connects with leadership measurement, talent management, succession, performance, and organizational change.
  • Assessment and coaching: Knowledge of leadership assessment, psychometrics, feedback, and coaching, including their appropriate use and limitations in development and talent decisions.
  • Engagement management and economics: Understanding of scoping, work planning, resourcing, budget management, change control, and profitability.
  • Client relationship development: Understanding of executive stakeholder management, client experience, and how demonstrated impact supports retention and account expansion.

Skills

  • Leadership development design: Creates coherent development journeys that connect individual insight, shared learning, workplace application, and measurement.
  • Executive facilitation: Leads senior groups, manages challenging dynamics, and helps participants reach decisions and commit to action.
  • Engagement management: Converts objectives into an executable plan and manages quality, scope, resources, timelines, and economics.
  • Executive relationship development: Builds credibility through insight, sound judgment, responsiveness, and reliable delivery; navigates stakeholder dynamics and handles difficult conversations constructively.
  • Communication and synthesis: Translates complex evidence into clear narratives, practical recommendations, and useful executive discussions.
  • Assessment and developmental feedback: Interprets assessment evidence and translates it into constructive feedback and actionable development priorities.
  • Solution design and commercial support: Contributes specialist expertise to sales discussions and develops practical approaches, scopes, resource estimates, and pricing recommendations.
  • Team leadership: Sets clear expectations, delegates effectively, and provides feedback that strengthens delivery and develops colleagues.

Experience

  • Progressive consulting or professional services experience, with substantial accountability for leading complete client engagements.
  • A strong record of designing and delivering leadership development programs, executive workshops, and leadership team effectiveness engagements.
  • Experience connecting leadership development with culture, organizational change, or broader talent priorities.
  • Accountability for engagement delivery, teams, budgets, resources, and profitability.
  • Experience building trusted relationships with executive sponsors and senior stakeholders across functions.
  • Evidence of sustained client relationships, repeat engagements, or expansion arising from successful delivery.
  • Experience contributing as a subject matter expert to sales discussions, solution design, proposals, scoping, and pricing.
  • Experience leading and developing consulting colleagues and coordinating specialist contributors.
  • Experience incorporating assessment and feedback into leadership development; direct executive assessment experience is an advantage.
  • Experience across at least two industries, ideally including large or global organizations.
  • Experience developing cohort-based leadership programs or executive academies is an advantage.

Competencies

  • Earns Trust: Builds credibility through integrity, transparency, and consistent follow-through, demonstrating reliability in commitments and creating confidence in their intent and actions.
  • Accelerates Performance: Drives consistent execution against goals by setting clear expectations, aligning resources, monitoring progress, and ensuring accountability for measurable outcomes.
  • Navigates Complexity: Structures ambiguous, multifaceted, or poorly defined problems into clear components, identifies key drivers and interdependencies, and creates clarity where none exists.
  • Situational Agility: Adjusts interpersonal approach, communication style, and leadership behaviors in response to differing people, contexts, and situational demands to maintain effectiveness and alignment.
  • Develops People: Builds capability in others through coaching, feedback, delegation of stretch opportunities, and intentional development planning that strengthens performance and readiness for future roles.
  • Seeks Diverse Perspectives: Actively solicits, listens to, and integrates input from individuals with varied experiences, expertise, and viewpoints to improve thinking, challenge assumptions, and strengthen decisions.

Attributes

  • Learning Orientation: A tendency to seek out perspectives that challenge existing assumptions, explore new ideas and methods, and use those insights to improve performance and address emerging problems.
  • Confidence: A stable belief in one’s ability to lead effectively, reflected in assured decision-making, self-trust, and comfort taking responsibility.
  • Resilience: An underlying capacity to recover quickly from setbacks and maintain emotional steadiness and optimism through uncertainty.
  • Integrity: An internalized commitment to aligning values and actions in service of others' genuine well-being.
  • Humility: A tendency to view oneself with grounded perspective, acknowledging limitations and valuing others’ contributions. Reflects an inclination to share credit, stay open to being wrong, and prioritize learning and collective success over personal ego.
  • Compassion: A tendency to understand others’ experiences while maintaining enough emotional clarity to offer grounded support. Reflects an inclination toward care paired with appropriate boundaries, accountability, and effective action.

Education and Professional Qualifications

  • Relevant degree or equivalent professional experience.
  • An advanced degree in organizational psychology, industrial-organizational psychology, organizational development, or a related field is preferred.
  • Relevant coaching qualifications and assessment certifications are valued, with appropriate accreditation required for any specialist tools or services delivered.

Why Modern?

Purpose-Driven Work: Join a team that is committed to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) and gives back to the community by donating 10% of annual profits to support underserved youth and educational opportunities.

Impactful Projects: Contribute to meaningful projects that positively impact clients’ organizations, communities, and the development of diverse leaders.

Professional Growth: Gain exposure to various aspects of the business, with opportunities for mentorship, leadership development, and career advancement.

Comprehensive Benefits: Enjoy a robust benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision insurance, along with a 401(k) match.

Flexibility & Balance: Benefit from a flexible remote work environment, paid parental leave, and an office setup stipend to support your work-from-home needs.

Our Values

Be Bold: Think strategically, seeing implications and creative paths. Innovates commercially – seeks to understand client perspective to drive impact. Innovates internally - seeks to improve processes, procedures, and technology used within and across their teams. 

Be Excellent: Deliver client ready work, with attention to detail, raising the bar of expectations within team and with data integrity to include the use of all company tools and systems. Motivated by excellence to the benefit of clients and our firm.  

Be United: Be an inclusive ‘team player,’ willing to support, develop and ‘go the extra mile’ to deliver impact with others. Proactively develops trusting relationships both within and outside our firm.  

Be Authentic: Demonstrate awareness, coachability and a desire to grow with continuous improvement. Motivated by a personal purpose aligned with our firm’s mission and values. Is accountable for delivery of client ready work. 

The pay range for this role is $185,000–$215,000 USD per year — Remote, United States.

Modern Executive Solutions is dedicated to creating an inclusive environment for everyone, regardless of ethnicity, religion, color, sexual orientation, gender identity, race, national origin, age, disability status, veteran or military status or care-giver status. jobs.excerpt: ABOUT SLATEAt Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization.
jobs.description:
ABOUT SLATE

At Slate, we’re building safe, reliable vehicles that people can afford, personalize and love—and doing it here in the USA as part of our commitment to reindustrialization. The spirit of DIY and customization runs throughout every element of a Slate, because people should have control over how their trucks look, feel, and represent them.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

Slate is looking for a seasoned, relationship-driven Business Development Manager, Federal to lead our federal vehicle sales efforts. As an individual contributor on the Fleet Sales team, you will own Slate’s pursuit of federal government business, including civilian agencies, the Department of Defense and the military services, and the GSA vehicle acquisition channel. You will bring established relationships and deep procurement know-how to open doors, navigate long and complex buying cycles, and convert them into awarded contracts and delivered vehicles.

As one of Slate’s first fleet sales leaders, you will help build the federal business from the ground up. You will act as a trusted advisor to fleet managers, contracting officers, and program leaders, guiding them through the transition to electric vehicles with Slate’s truck, accessories, and related fleet solutions.

WHAT YOU GET TO DO

  • Own the federal pipeline end to end, from account planning and opportunity identification through solicitation response, award, and delivery handoff.
  • Develop and execute a strategic account plan for priority federal customers across civilian agencies, DoD, and the military services, including installation and base-level fleet managers.
  • Navigate federal acquisition channels, including GSA Schedule and GSA Fleet / Automotive, agency-direct purchasing, and military procurement vehicles, and guide Slate’s path to the right contract vehicles.
  • Lead pursuit of solicitations, RFIs, RFQs, and RFPs, partnering with Legal, Finance, Pricing, and Operations on proposals, compliance requirements, and pricing.
  • Build and sustain senior-level relationships with fleet managers, contracting officers, program offices, and prime or channel partners.
  • Represent Slate at federal-focused events, industry days, conferences, and customer demos.
  • Translate federal requirements and mandates, such as fleet electrification goals, domestic-content and Buy American considerations, and charging infrastructure needs, into compelling value propositions for Slate vehicles.
  • Maintain an accurate pipeline and forecast in Salesforce, and meet or exceed unit and revenue targets in a long-cycle, high-value deal environment.
  • Serve as the voice of the federal customer, bringing market and requirements feedback to Fleet Sales leadership, Product, and Engineering.
  • Collaborate with Fleet Sales colleagues, Fleet Customer Success, Marketing, and Digital to deliver a best-in-class customer experience.

WHAT YOU BRING TO THE TEAM

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Public Policy, or a related field. Advanced degree is preferred.
  • 8+ years of direct experience in automotive or EV fleet sales, serving government, public-sector, and commercial (B2B) customers.
  • 2+ years of direct experience in government fleet sales, with demonstrated success selling to federal agencies, navigating complex public-sector procurement processes, closing large federal deals, and meeting or exceeding quota.
  • Hands-on experience navigating federal and military procurement, including GSA schedules and contract vehicles, FAR / DFARS fundamentals, and agency-specific purchasing processes.
  • Established relationships with federal fleet, procurement, or contracting stakeholders, including DoD and military services, are strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated success managing multi-stakeholder sales cycles that span many months or years.
  • Highly motivated, gritty self-starter who can operate in a dynamic white-space environment and work through roadblocks. You’re a hunter, not a farmer.
  • Exceptional communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with a consultative sales approach.
  • Proficiency using Salesforce or other CRM systems.
  • Proficiency using Microsoft Office (Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Active security clearance is a plus, but not required.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Must have the ability to travel (up to 50%).
  • Must have the ability to lift up to 35 pounds.
  • Must have the ability to stand, walk, and perform repetitive tasks for extended periods.

SALARY RANGE

The compensation for this position is the range Slate reasonably and in good faith expects to pay for the position taking into account the wide variety of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including job-related knowledge; skillset; experience, education and training; certifications; work location; and other relevant business and organizational factors.


Annual Base Pay Range: $114,612 to $203,335 USD


ADDITIONAL COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

Slate offers a wide range of competitive benefits, including medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, vacation, and 401k. The successful candidate may also be eligible to participate in the equity program and/or a discretionary annual incentive program, subject to the rules governing such programs.


WORK AUTHORIZATION REQUIREMENT

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States on a permanent basis. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship at this time.

WHY JOIN TEAM SLATE?

At Slate, we’re fueled by grit, determination, and attention to detail. The start-up spirit of ingenuity and resourcefulness move our business forward. Team Slate fosters a culture of excellence, innovation, and mutual respect, and is motivated by shared principles.

  • Safety First

  • Delight Customers

  • One Team

  • Relentless Improvement

  • Fast, Frugal, and Scrappy

  • Respectful Collaboration

  • Positive Legacy

WE WANT TO WORK WITH PEOPLE THAT REFLECT THE COMMUNITIES IN WHICH WE OPERATE.

Slate is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. jobs.title: Director, Human Resources
jobs.excerpt: The Opportunity Landmark Ventures is seeking an exceptional Director, Human Resources to help build, develop, and support the team that drives our business forward.
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Landmark Ventures is seeking an exceptional Director, Human Resources to help build, develop, and support the team that drives our business forward.


This is a hands-on role at the intersection of talent acquisition, people development, and HR leadership. We are looking for someone who is equally energized by finding extraordinary people, helping existing employees reach their potential, and building the systems, policies, and practices that make a growing organization work better.


At its core, this is a role focused on three things: bringing great people into Landmark, making the people already here better, and ensuring we have an effective and well-run HR function.


The Director will lead Landmark’s recruiting efforts, help strengthen performance and professional development across the organization, and oversee the HR operations, employee relations, policies, and processes that support our people and culture.


Landmark is an entrepreneurial organization with multiple businesses, a distributed workforce, and an ambitious vision for growth. Our people are central to everything we do, and we need an HR leader who understands that recruiting, developing, and retaining exceptional talent are among the most important investments we can make.


This person will partner closely with the COO, executive leadership, practice leaders, and our HR/Ops team to translate that belief into action.


And in a world where AI and modern technology are changing how companies recruit, develop, and manage talent, we want someone who is curious, forward-thinking, and eager to use these tools to make our HR function smarter, faster, and more effective without losing the human judgment and relationships that matter most.


Key Responsibilities

  1. Talent Acquisition & Recruiting (50%)
Identify, attract, and hire exceptional people who can move our organization forward.

Recruiting is one of the most important responsibilities of this role. We want someone who sees talent acquisition not simply as filling open positions, but as building the future of the organization.
  • Own and lead Landmark’s overall recruiting strategy and talent acquisition process across our businesses and teams.
  • Serve as a hands-on recruiter, actively sourcing, identifying, engaging, screening, and evaluating candidates for positions across the organization.
  • Partner with hiring managers to understand business needs, define roles, develop compelling job descriptions, establish candidate profiles, and determine what exceptional talent looks like for each position.
  • Build and maintain strong candidate pipelines, including proactive outreach and relationship development with prospective candidates before positions become available.
  • Lead recruiting efforts from initial sourcing and candidate engagement through interviews, assessments, reference checks, offers, and hiring decisions.
  • Develop thoughtful interview processes, evaluation frameworks, and selection criteria that help managers make better, more consistent hiring decisions.
  • Help hiring managers become more effective interviewers and evaluators of talent.
  • Identify and recommend new recruiting channels, platforms, communities, networks, and approaches to reach high-quality candidates.
  • Oversee recruiting platforms, applicant tracking systems, and candidate communications to ensure an organized, efficient, and positive candidate experience.
  • Partner with leadership on workforce planning, organizational needs, future hiring priorities, and the capabilities Landmark will need as we grow.
  • Establish and monitor recruiting metrics, including time-to-fill, pipeline quality, hiring effectiveness, and candidate experience.
  • Direct and coordinate recruiting activities with the HR Assistant and other internal team members while maintaining personal ownership of recruiting outcomes.
  • Continuously improve how Landmark identifies, attracts, evaluates, and hires talent.

The goal is not simply to fill positions. The goal is to consistently bring people into Landmark who raise the bar for everyone around them.


We want someone who enjoys recruiting, is good at recognizing talent, and takes real satisfaction in finding the right person for the right opportunity.


Sometimes that means developing a thoughtful hiring strategy for a senior leadership position. Sometimes it means sourcing candidates directly, reviewing applications, conducting interviews, or helping a manager recognize that the best candidate may not have the most conventional background. You should be comfortable doing all of it.

  1. Talent Development & Organizational Performance (30%)
Help make Landmark a place where talented people continually grow, managers become stronger leaders, and teams perform at their best.


Hiring great people is only the beginning. We want an HR leader who is equally committed to helping employees develop their capabilities, advance their careers, and do the best work of their lives.


This is not simply about coordinating training sessions or administering performance reviews. It is about building a culture where development is intentional, feedback is meaningful, and people are continually getting better.


Performance Management & Employee Growth

  • Own and continually improve Landmark’s performance management approach, ensuring employees receive clear expectations, meaningful feedback, and opportunities to grow.
  • Lead the effective use of Lattice, including Reviews, Updates, and Grow, as tools for ongoing performance, feedback, and professional development.
  • Manage biannual performance review cycles, including planning, communications, manager preparation, calibration, promotion discussions, and follow-up.
  • Partner with managers to strengthen the quality and consistency of employee feedback, coaching, and performance conversations.
  • Help employees and managers establish meaningful professional development goals and actionable growth plans.
  • Oversee and evolve Landmark’s Career Tracks and Grow Areas across practices, ensuring employees understand expectations, competencies, and opportunities for advancement.
  • Identify employees with strong potential and partner with leadership to create development opportunities, stretch assignments, and pathways for increased responsibility.
  • Help managers address underperformance constructively, consistently, and effectively.
  • Establish systems that turn performance conversations into meaningful action rather than administrative exercises.

Learning, Professional Development & Manager Effectiveness

  • Develop and lead Landmark’s professional development strategy, connecting employee learning with organizational needs and business priorities.
  • Identify the skills, capabilities, and competencies employees need to succeed in their current roles and prepare for future opportunities.
  • Design and coordinate high-value professional development sessions, workshops, learning experiences, and other opportunities for employees across the organization.
  • Develop practical manager training programs focused on coaching, communication, delegation, accountability, performance management, and team leadership.
  • Partner with internal subject matter experts and external resources to create relevant, engaging, and useful learning experiences.
  • Build and strengthen mentorship, peer learning, knowledge sharing, and other employee development initiatives.
  • Help managers translate employee development needs into specific actions, experiences, and opportunities.
  • Evaluate the effectiveness of learning and development initiatives and continuously refine programs based on employee needs and organizational outcomes.

Employee Engagement, Culture & Organizational Health

  • Lead initiatives that strengthen employee engagement, organizational health, retention, and the overall employee experience.
  • Oversee employee feedback and organizational health surveys, identifying meaningful patterns, opportunities, and areas requiring attention.
  • Partner with leadership and managers to translate employee feedback into practical improvements and measurable action plans.
  • Support recognition, employee milestones, appreciation, and other programs that reinforce Landmark’s culture.
  • Help identify retention risks and develop thoughtful strategies to keep talented employees engaged and growing.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, including the IDEA Council and related inclusion and belonging programs.
  • Partner with leadership to strengthen collaboration, communication, accountability, and employee connection across our distributed organization.

The goal is to create an environment where people know what great performance looks like, understand how to get there, and have the support to keep improving.


We want someone who recognizes that a performance review is only valuable if it changes something. That professional development is not simply about offering classes, but about building capabilities. And that a great manager can have an extraordinary impact on an employee’s experience, growth, and long-term success. Your job is to help make those things happen across Landmark.

  1. HR Operations, Policies & Employee Relations (20%)
Build and maintain a thoughtful, efficient, and well-run HR function that supports our employees, managers, and business.


A great HR function needs strong fundamentals. Policies should be clear. Processes should work. Employee concerns should be addressed thoughtfully and promptly. Managers should know where to turn for guidance. And employees should feel that HR is professional, responsive, consistent, and fair.


We want someone who can oversee these responsibilities with confidence and sound judgment while building systems that make the organization easier to operate as we grow.


HR Policies, Compliance & Employee Relations

  • Own and maintain Landmark’s HR policies, procedures, employee handbook, and related employment practices.
  • Ensure HR practices align with applicable employment laws, regulations, and company requirements, coordinating with external HR, legal, and compliance resources as appropriate.
  • Serve as a trusted resource to employees and managers on HR policies, employee concerns, workplace expectations, and people-related issues.
  • Partner with leadership and managers to address employee relations matters, performance concerns, workplace conflicts, and other sensitive situations thoughtfully and consistently.
  • Provide practical guidance on employee documentation, corrective actions, performance improvement plans, and other personnel matters.
  • Identify potential HR risks, recommend appropriate actions, and help resolve issues before they escalate.
  • Oversee required employee training, policy acknowledgments, and compliance-related initiatives.
  • Maintain appropriate confidentiality, professionalism, and discretion in all employee matters.

HR Systems, Administration & Employee Lifecycle

  • Oversee the effective administration of Landmark’s HR systems, including BambooHR, Lattice, recruiting platforms, and related tools.
  • Lead the overall onboarding process, ensuring new employees have an organized, welcoming, and productive transition into Landmark.
  • Partner with hiring managers and the HR/Ops team to establish meaningful onboarding experiences and clear expectations for employees’ first 30, 60, and 90 days.
  • Oversee employee lifecycle processes, including new-hire documentation, employee changes, promotions, departures, and related HR administration.
  • Ensure employee records, HR documentation, and personnel information are accurate, current, secure, and appropriately maintained.
  • Coordinate with the HR/Ops team and external partners on benefits administration, employee questions, and related HR processes.
  • Develop and maintain clear HR workflows, documentation, responsibilities, and operating procedures.
  • Partner with the HR Assistant and Senior Assistant to ensure day-to-day HR activities are completed accurately, consistently, and on time.
  • Establish and maintain useful HR dashboards and reporting, including headcount, turnover, retention, hiring effectiveness, performance, engagement, and other relevant people metrics.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and improve administrative processes so HR can spend more time on higher-value work.

HR Communications & Organizational Support

  • Oversee clear, timely, and professional employee communications related to policies, benefits, onboarding, employee programs, and organizational updates.
  • Coordinate HR communications across Slack, Lattice, and other appropriate channels.
  • Partner with leadership to identify organizational needs, emerging people challenges, and opportunities to strengthen the employee experience.
  • Help ensure HR practices and programs are applied consistently across Landmark’s businesses and distributed teams.

The goal is not to create more HR bureaucracy. The goal is to create an HR function that works exceptionally well, gives managers and employees the support they need, and allows the organization to focus on doing great work.


Sometimes that means resolving a sensitive employee issue. Sometimes it means rewriting a confusing policy, fixing a broken onboarding process, or introducing a better system. You should be comfortable moving between the details and the bigger picture.


Leadership & Strategic Partnership


Across all three areas, the Director will serve as Landmark’s primary HR leader and a trusted partner to the COO, executive leadership, and department managers.

  • Translate Landmark’s business priorities into practical recruiting, talent development, and HR initiatives.
  • Provide leadership with thoughtful recommendations on hiring, employee performance, retention, organizational effectiveness, and workforce planning.
  • Take ownership of HR priorities and drive projects from initial idea through implementation and ongoing improvement.
  • Lead and coordinate the work of the HR/Ops team, establishing clear responsibilities, expectations, and accountability.
  • Balance the needs of employees, managers, and the business while maintaining fairness, sound judgment, and professionalism.
  • Identify opportunities to improve how Landmark recruits, develops, manages, and supports its people.
  • Bring forward solutions rather than simply identifying problems.

We want someone who can operate independently, make good decisions, and know when to involve leadership. Someone who understands that HR is not a separate administrative function operating alongside the business. It is an essential part of how we build a better business.


AI, Technology & Modern HR


Help Landmark develop a smarter, more effective, and increasingly AI-enabled approach to recruiting, talent development, and HR operations.

  • Use modern AI tools to support candidate research, sourcing, job description development, interview preparation, recruiting communications, and other talent acquisition activities.
  • Explore how AI can improve professional development, manager resources, training materials, employee communications, and HR workflows.
  • Identify opportunities to automate repetitive administrative tasks and improve the quality and efficiency of HR operations.
  • Develop practical tools, templates, and processes that help managers and employees navigate common HR activities more effectively.
  • Apply strong judgment to ensure AI-supported processes remain accurate, fair, confidential, and appropriately human-centered.
  • Stay current with emerging HR technologies, recruiting approaches, and people development practices.

Technology should help us spend less time on repetitive work and more time finding great people, developing talent, and solving meaningful organizational challenges. We want someone who understands that distinction.


Qualifications & Experience

The ideal candidate will bring:

  • 7-10+ years of progressive HR experience, including substantial hands-on experience in recruiting, talent development, performance management, and HR operations.
  • Ability to work independently while leveraging the strengths of a small, collaborative team, with a willingness and comfort to drive hands-on execution.
  • Demonstrated success directly recruiting and hiring talented professionals across multiple functions and levels, including senior-level positions.
  • Strong recruiting instincts and the ability to identify, engage, evaluate, and attract exceptional candidates.
  • Experience building and managing recruiting pipelines, sourcing strategies, interview processes, and applicant tracking systems.
  • Demonstrated experience developing employee performance management, professional development, and manager training programs.
  • Strong understanding of employee relations, HR policies, employment practices, and compliance requirements.
  • Experience partnering directly with senior executives and department managers on people-related decisions and organizational priorities.
  • Experience with HRIS, ATS, and performance management platforms, including systems such as BambooHR and Lattice.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to use recruiting, performance, and organizational data to inform decisions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to handle sensitive conversations thoughtfully and effectively.
  • Strong project management skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities across a fast-moving organization.
  • High levels of initiative, ownership, organization, and attention to detail.
  • Sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to handle confidential employee information appropriately.
  • Comfort working across a distributed organization with employees and teams in different locations.
  • Curiosity and fluency with modern AI tools and technology-enabled HR workflows.
  • A bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

HR certifications such as SHRM-CP, SHRM-SCP, PHR, or SPHR are a plus. Experience in professional services, consulting, technology, or a similarly entrepreneurial environment is particularly valuable, as is experience working with remote or international teams.


The Person We’re Looking For


We’re looking for someone who is equal parts recruiter, talent developer, and HR leader.


Your career may have started in recruiting, human resources, talent management, organizational development, or a combination of these areas. What matters is that you are someone who genuinely enjoys working with people and understands how to translate that interest into better hiring decisions, stronger employee performance, and a healthier organization.


You are a recruiter at heart. You enjoy finding people. You know how to search beyond the obvious candidates. You can recognize potential, ask thoughtful questions, and help hiring managers distinguish between someone who interviews well and someone who will actually perform well. You understand that great talent rarely appears simply because a job has been posted.


You are also passionate about helping people get better. You can look across an organization and identify where managers need more support, where employees need clearer development opportunities, and where the right training, coaching, or feedback could make a meaningful difference. You believe performance management should be about improving performance, not simply documenting it.


You are comfortable having difficult conversations. You can help a manager address an underperforming employee. You can listen carefully to an employee concern, separate facts from assumptions, and recommend a thoughtful path forward. You understand that fairness, consistency, and good judgment matter.


You can also build systems. You can look at a recruiting process, onboarding experience, performance review cycle, or HR policy and recognize where it is unnecessarily complicated, inefficient, or simply not working as well as it should. And you know how to make it better.
You don’t need a large team to be effective. You are comfortable leading others, but you’re equally willing to roll up your sleeves and do the work yourself.


You can move between a senior-level recruiting search, a manager coaching conversation, an employee relations issue, and an HR process improvement without losing sight of what matters most.


You are proactive rather than reactive. You have high standards, but you are practical. You understand that policies and processes are important, but they exist to support people and the business, not the other way around.


And most importantly, you understand that the quality of an organization is ultimately shaped by the people it brings in, the opportunities it creates for them to grow, and the environment in which they do their work. Your job is to help Landmark get better at all three.


Work Environment & Compensation


Landmark Ventures is headquartered in New York City and operates as a remote-first organization with a distributed team. While our core working hours often align with the East Coast, we offer flexibility and accommodate team members across different time zones.

Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States.


About Our Benefits

  • Competitive compensation with opportunities to be recognized and rewarded for individual performance and contributions.
  • A flexible, remote-first working environment with colleagues across the United States and internationally.
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, vision, and life insurance through ADP, with employees contributing just $1 per month for coverage.
  • A collaborative, entrepreneurial team with an engaged virtual culture, active Slack communities, and regular in-person and virtual gatherings.
  • Meaningful professional development opportunities, career conversations, learning experiences, external resources, and stretch assignments.
  • The opportunity to work alongside experienced colleagues, ambitious entrepreneurs, and innovative clients across multiple industries.

About Landmark Ventures


For more than 25 years, Landmark Ventures has worked with extraordinary founders, brands, and enterprises to realize their growth ambitions. We help organizations reach new customers, enter new markets, build strategic relationships, accelerate pipelines, create extraordinary events and experiences, execute M&A transactions, raise capital, and unlock new opportunities.


Today, Landmark operates across multiple businesses, events, communities, and emerging brands, creating an unusually rich environment for someone who is passionate about finding great people, developing talent, and helping an entrepreneurial organization grow.


Landmark Ventures is committed to hiring a diverse team that provides important perspectives in our work and is an equal opportunity employer that welcomes all qualified applicants regardless of race, ethnicity, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, physical or mental ability, gender identity or expression, or veteran status.

jobs.description:
über uns

Was für einen Kunden eine Ausnahme ist, gehört für den nächsten zum Tagesgeschäft. Wir entwickeln Individualsoftware für mittelständische Unternehmen aus Industrie, Handel und Versicherungen. Gemeinsam betreuen wir mehrere Kundenprojekte - so lernst du unterschiedliche Geschäftsabläufe kennen und gestaltest Anwendungen für Web, Mobilgeräte und Desktop.
Als Senior Software Engineer klärst du mit den Fachleuten auf Kundenseite, was die Software im Alltag leisten muss. Du gestaltest die Architektur mit und setzt deine Entscheidungen selbst im Code um.

das gibt es zu tun

  • Fachliche Anforderungen verstehen. Du klärst mit den Fachleuten auf Kundenseite, welche Abläufe die Anwendung unterstützen soll. Du übersetzt Geschäftsregeln und Sonderfälle in ein tragfähiges Softwaredesign.
  • Architektur gestalten und selbst entwickeln. Du entscheidest mit, wie eine Anwendung aufgebaut ist, wie ihre Komponenten zusammenspielen und wo sie an bestehende Systeme angebunden wird. Deine Entscheidungen bringst du selbst in den Code.
  • Anwendungen durchgängig entwickeln.Je nach Projekt entwickelst du Geschäftslogik und Schnittstellen mit C# und .NET oder mit TypeScript und Node.js. Dabei arbeitest du an Webanwendungen ebenso wie an nativen Apps für Mobilgeräte oder Desktop.
  • Mit Daten arbeiten. Du entwirfst relationale Datenmodelle, die fachliche Zusammenhänge verständlich abbilden. Wenn eine Abfrage mit wachsender Datenmenge langsam wird, gehst du der Ursache auf den Grund.
  • Bestehende Software weiterentwickeln. Du findest Wege, neue Anforderungen sauber in eine gewachsene Codebasis zu integrieren. In Code-Reviews teilst du deine Erfahrung und machst technische Entscheidungen im Team nachvollziehbar.

das bringst du mit

  • Du hast mindestens fünf Jahre Erfahrung in der professionellen Softwareentwicklung. Besonders wertvoll ist für uns, wenn du bereits Individualsoftware für Kunden entwickelt oder an komplexen Fachanwendungen gearbeitet hast.
  • Du bringst ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Informatik, Informationstechnik oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation mit.
  • Dein technischer Schwerpunkt liegt in C# und .NET oder in TypeScript und Node.js. In einem der beiden Stacks hast du fundierte Praxiserfahrung, mit dem anderen hast du bereits gearbeitet.
  • Kenntnisse in Vue.js, React oder Angular sind ebenso willkommen wie Erfahrung mit nativen Mobil- oder Desktop-Anwendungen. Java-Kenntnisse sind ein weiteres Plus.
  • Du hast Erfahrung mit Softwarearchitektur, wendest Clean-Code-Prinzipien an und kannst begründen, wann ein Entwurfsmuster ein konkretes Problem einfacher löst.
  • Du kennst dich gut mit relationalen Datenbanken aus und hast praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens einem dieser Systeme gesammelt – PostgreSQL, Microsoft SQL Server, Oracle oder IBM DB2.
  • Du bist offen für moderne Entwicklungswerkzeuge und Agentic Coding. Du hast Lust, Coding-Agenten gezielt einzusetzen, und prüfst ihre Vorschläge mit demselben Anspruch wie deinen eigenen Code.
  • Du kannst technische Entscheidungen im Team und gegenüber Kunden verständlich erklären.
  • Du kommunizierst sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch

das bekommst du

  • Start & Welcoming so wie du es verdienst! Ein strukturiertes Onboarding mit echten Ansprechpersonen - damit du vom ersten Tag an durchstartest.
  • Remote Work Homeoffice innerhalb von Deutschland oder Arbeiten in unserem modernen Büro in Offenburg? Arbeite so, wie es für dich am besten passt.
  • AI-first arbeiten, statt darüber zu reden Lizenzen für Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot & Co. stellen wir. Neue Tools und Modelle darfst du ausprobieren, statt sie zu beantragen – und deine Erkenntnisse verändern, wie das ganze Team arbeitet. 
  • Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit 20 % Arbeitgeberzuschuss - deutlich über dem gesetzlichen Standard.
  • Du entscheidest ob Hansefit-Mitgliedschaft oder 50 € monatlich per Spendit Card - dein Benefit, deine Wahl.

Campaign Planning & Delivery

KPIs

If you thrive in high-pressure environments where urgency meets creativity and where every challenge is an opportunity to create impact, then continue reading....

Lenders Cooperative seeks an SBA Closing Specialist who willassist the lender by preparing and reviewing loan closing documentation for compliance with SBA 7(a) guidelines, policies, and procedures. This role involves verifying that all loan approval conditions have been met, coordinating with borrowers and third parties, and ensuring the accuracy and completeness of closing packages. The SBA Closing Specialist ensures all documents align with SBA SOP requirements and lender standards. Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and knowledge of the SBA 7(a) program are essential for success in this position.

Key Objectives

  • Loan Documentation Preparation: Prepare and review SBA loan closing documents for compliance with SBA guidelines and lender requirements, ensuring accuracy and completeness in every document.
  • Loan Processing and Packaging: Compile and organize loan application documents, such as financial statements, tax returns, and personal financial statements, into complete and compliant loan packages for SBA submission and review. Ensure packages meet SBA standards and address any documentation gaps or inconsistencies.
  • Coordination and Communication: Act as a primary contact for borrowers, lenders, and third parties (e.g., title companies, attorneys) throughout the loan process. Provide updates, answer questions, and coordinate documentation to ensure smooth transitions across application, processing, and closing stages.
  • Review and Analysis of Loan Packages: Analyze borrower information and supporting documents, including purchase agreements, budgets, and FF&E costs, to validate the loan's intended purpose and sources/uses of funds.
  • Closing Process Management: Manage the closing timeline by tracking loan status and following up with internal and external parties to ensure closing deadlines are met. Confirm all closing conditions are satisfied and coordinate the preparation of final closing documents for borrower signatures.
  • Compliance and Regulatory Checks: Perform and/or review compliance checks, including CAIVRS for federal debt delinquencies and SAM.gov reports for debarment status. Ensure all parties involved are eligible to conduct business with the federal government.
  • Coordination with Underwriting Team: Collaborate with underwriters to address pre-closing requirements, including handling additional documentation requests or issues to maintain compliance with SBA and lender policies.

jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly skilled and proactive Digital Site Reliability Engineer (Digital SRE) to ensure the reliability, availability, performance, and scalability of our digital platforms, websites, applications, APIs, and customer-facing services.

The successful candidate will combine software engineering, cloud infrastructure, automation, and operational excellence to improve digital service performance and minimize downtime. This role will focus on monitoring digital experiences, preventing service disruptions, automating operational processes, and collaborating with development, DevOps, cybersecurity, and product teams to deliver seamless digital experiences.

The ideal candidate will have a strong background in site reliability engineering, cloud platforms, application performance monitoring, incident management, and digital service optimization.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain the availability, reliability, and performance of websites, web applications, APIs, and other digital services.
  • Monitor digital platforms using observability, logging, tracing, and application performance monitoring tools.
  • Identify and resolve production incidents, service interruptions, latency issues, and performance bottlenecks.
  • Establish and maintain service-level indicators (SLIs), service-level objectives (SLOs), and service-level agreements (SLAs).
  • Automate repetitive operational tasks, deployment processes, monitoring activities, and incident response workflows.
  • Collaborate with software developers, DevOps engineers, and product teams to improve application reliability and deployment quality.
  • Manage and optimize cloud infrastructure across AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • Support containerized applications and orchestration platforms such as Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Conduct root cause analysis and implement corrective and preventive measures following service incidents.
  • Design and maintain scalable, fault-tolerant architectures for customer-facing digital platforms.
  • Optimize application response times, server utilization, availability, and overall user experience.
  • Implement and maintain CI/CD pipelines, infrastructure as code, and automated testing practices.
  • Develop dashboards, alerts, and reporting mechanisms to identify potential service degradation before it affects customers.
  • Support disaster recovery planning, backup procedures, resilience testing, and business continuity initiatives.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and coordinate incident response when required.
  • Maintain technical documentation, operational runbooks, system architecture diagrams, and reliability reports.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Three or more years of experience in site reliability engineering, DevOps, cloud engineering, production operations, or a related role.
  • Strong understanding of web technologies, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, APIs, networking, and distributed systems.
  • Experience with cloud infrastructure and services, preferably AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.
  • Proficiency in scripting or programming languages such as Python, Go, Bash, or similar.
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tools such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, New Relic, or Splunk.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, or comparable platforms.
  • Experience with Linux administration, containerization, and infrastructure automation.
  • Knowledge of incident management, root cause analysis, and production troubleshooting.
  • Understanding of high availability, scalability, fault tolerance, and disaster recovery principles.
  • Strong analytical, communication, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting high-traffic websites, e-commerce platforms, digital products, or customer-facing applications.
  • Knowledge of Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, and Infrastructure as Code.
  • Experience with application performance monitoring, distributed tracing, and centralized logging.
  • Familiarity with digital experience monitoring, real-user monitoring (RUM), and synthetic monitoring.
  • Knowledge of security best practices, vulnerability management, and cloud security controls.
  • Experience with reliability testing, chaos engineering, load testing, and performance optimization.
  • Relevant certifications in AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Kubernetes, or site reliability engineering.

Compensation and Benefits

The anticipated salary range for this position is $115,000–$165,000 annually for a full-time role in the United States. Candidates with extensive experience managing large-scale digital platforms, cloud-native applications, automation, and production reliability may qualify for compensation toward the upper end of the range.

Actual compensation will depend on the candidate's technical skills, years of experience, location, responsibilities, and the employer's compensation structure.

Depending on the employer, benefits may include:

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
  • Paid vacation, holidays, and sick leave.
  • Retirement savings plans with employer contributions, where available.
  • Professional development and certification reimbursement.
  • Remote or hybrid work flexibility, where applicable.
  • Performance-based bonuses or other incentives, where offered.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Performance may be measured using the following metrics:

  • Digital platform uptime and service availability.
  • Mean time to detect (MTTD) and mean time to recover (MTTR).
  • Application response times, latency, and error rates.
  • Achievement of established SLIs, SLOs, and SLAs.
  • Reduction in production incidents and unplanned downtime.
  • Deployment success rates and change failure rates.
  • Effectiveness of monitoring, automation, and incident prevention.
  • Customer-facing digital service performance and reliability.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a technically proficient and reliability-focused professional who understands the relationship between infrastructure performance and digital user experience. They should be proactive in identifying risks, comfortable responding to production incidents, and capable of using automation and monitoring data to improve service reliability.

The successful candidate will demonstrate strong collaboration skills, a continuous improvement mindset, and the ability to maintain dependable digital services in a fast-paced environment.

Position Overview

Netwrix is seeking a proactive and driven Federal Sales Account Executive to identify, engage, land and expand new business across DoD, Federal Civilian, Defense Contractor, and State, Local, and Education (SLED) accounts in the Mid-Atlantic region. This is a high-impact role focused on generating pipeline, building executive-level relationships, and driving strategic growth in the public sector.

You will be responsible for prospecting, positioning Netwrix’s industry-leading security solutions, and leading a value driven sales process that delivers value to new and existing customers from the first conversation.

Candidates must be located within a 30-mile radius of Washington, DC. This is a remote position with local travel to customer sites, partner meetings, and events as needed.

  • Identify and pursue new business opportunities across DoD, Federal Civilian, Defense Contractor, and SLED accounts in the Mid-Atlantic, leveraging Netwrix’s comprehensive product suite to drive net new customer acquisitions.

  • Develop and execute a territory plan to maximize revenue from both existing customers and new prospects across the Mid-Atlantic, aligning Netwrix’s capabilities with customer pain points such as data access governance, federal compliance mandates (e.g., NIST 800-53, CMMC), Zero Trust initiatives, and insider threat detection.

  • Strong understanding of information security concepts—particularly those relevant to Netwrix’s offerings—such as data classification, access management, auditing, and compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST 800-53/800-171, FISMA, FedRAMP, CMMC, Zero Trust).

  • Experience using CRM tools like Salesforce to track sales progress and manage accounts.
  • Active U.S. security clearance, or the ability to obtain one, is preferred but not required.

Our Values

  • Excellence - We set high standards and take pride in delivering exceptional results. We celebrate wins, seek constant improvement, and address shortcomings professionally.

  • Winning with Clear Thinking - We value clarity, find straightforward solutions to complex problems, and make swift, effective decisions.
  • Relentless Innovation - We continually seek better ways to serve our customers and stay ahead. We foster creative thinking, and we embrace new approaches.
  • Industry-Leading Expertise - We take pride in our expertise and continuously seek to learn and share knowledge, striving to be the trusted experts our customers rely on.
  • eXceptional Together - We believe in the power of collaboration and diverse perspectives. By valuing each other’s strengths, we achieve outcomes that surpass individual contributions.

Join us in a culture where integrity, respect, and hard work are foundational. Be part of a team dedicated to making a lasting impact.

Why You’ll Love Working at Netwrix

  • Competitive Health Benefits
  • Continuous Learning and Development Opportunities
  • Team-Oriented, Collaborative, and Innovative Work Environment
  • Regular Company Town Halls to Keep You Informed
